frozen: 2026-10-22, after the development run (choke_scores_dev.json) and before the check cells (Red Sea, onset 2023-12-11) were built, predicted or scored. Disclosure: before the freeze I printed check-period VALUES while building the data (weekly WCI composite and Shanghai-Rotterdam prints to Aug 2024 when testing the scraper; monthly import-price, HICP, PPI-freight and GSCPI columns Sep 2023 - Dec 2024 in a data audit; weekly Suez / Bab el-Mandeb / Cape / Panama container transits Nov 2023 - Feb 2024), and I know the Red Sea outcome from general knowledge. No check prediction was compared with an outcome before this freeze; all parameters below come from development data, published pre-event literature or physical route arithmetic, and the check was not used to choose them.

L1.input: transit-reduction path at the chokepoint: weekly mean container transits (PortWatch n_container), d_t = 1 - transits_t / mean of the 26 weeks before the onset week, clipped to [0,1]
L1.mechanism: K_t = e * phi * EWMA_{a=0.5}(d_t); ln(R_t/R_0) = beta * K_t; R_0 = mean of the last two prints before the onset week
L1.beta_source: log rate rise per unit of effective capacity absorbed: about 10 % of the global fleet absorbed by congestion in 2021-22 (Carson/Splash247 Jul 2021; Linerlytica Feb 2022, 2.53m TEU = 10 %) with WCI composite x3 to x7 on 2019; not fitted, no development event has an exposed container lane
L1.phi_source: extra days of the diversion over an ~84-day Asia-Europe round trip: +11 days each way (OECD: journey times +30-45 %) gives 1 - 84/106 = 0.21; Panama alternatives +15 % (assumed)
L1.exposure_note: the Shanghai-Rotterdam lane is the Asia-Europe lane itself; the composite shares are assumed (two of eight WCI routes are Asia-Europe, volume-weighted), not measured
L1.check_cells: wci_rtm and wci, each over the first 26 weeks and the first 52 weeks from the onset week (4 cells, one event)
L1.others: Chronos-2 and TiRex-2 on the last 156 weekly log prints before the onset (no transit information)

pass.skill: pooled MAE below engine-off AND below the better of Chronos-2 / TiRex-2

L2.input: REALISED monthly freight index (lnF: SCFI composite to 2023-03, WCI composite changes after) given; origin = last import-price month public on the onset date (month + 35 days); F_0 = mean ln F of the 3 months before the onset month
L2.M1: ln(P_t/P_0) = eps * sum_{k=0..6} w_k (ln F_{t-k} - ln F_0), w_k ~ exp(-k/2); eps = 0.065 (a doubling of container freight raises import prices 4.4-4.9 %: OECD 2021a, UNCTAD 2021, Carriere-Swallow et al. 2021; all before the Red Sea event). Import prices are CIF (STS regulation), so freight enters directly
L2.M2: eps and tau by least squares on development months 2010-02 to 2023-11 (excluding the held-out event window, onset-3 to end+12 months) with the EUR/USD change as control; eps clipped to [0, 0.3]. Reported as a rescue
L2.targets: PRC_IMP_NEU (imports from outside the euro area), EA20: consumer goods excluding food (CPA_MIG_COG_X_FOOD) and intermediate goods (CPA_MIG_ING)
L2.others: Chronos-2, TiRex-2 on the last 96 monthly log values

L3.input: REALISED consumer-goods import prices (monthly) given; origin = last HICP month public on the onset date (month + 17 days)
L3.M1: ln(H_t/H_0) = eta * sum_{k=0..12} v_k (ln P_{t-k} - ln P_0) + seasonal path; v gamma-shaped, mean lag 6 months; eta = 0.25 (OECD / UNCTAD: consumer prices +0.4-0.7 % per doubling of freight against +4.4-4.9 % for import prices, goods about 2.5x as import-intensive as the basket)
L3.M2: eta and mean lag (4,6,8,10) by least squares on development months, month dummies, eta clipped to [0, 0.6]
L3.target: HICP non-energy industrial goods (IGD_NNRG), euro area, index NSA; seasonal factors = centred mean m/m by calendar month over 8 years to the origin, removed from the realised path
L3.check_cells: one window, origin+1 to 2025-06 (HICP EA series ends 2025-12)
L3.others: Chronos-2, TiRex-2 on the last 96 monthly log values, net of the seasonal path

identification: a cell is 'detectable' if |realised window mean| > 2 SD of the same statistic over placebo windows of the same length in 2012-2019 (SCFI weekly for L1, import prices and HICP monthly for L2/L3). The chain is cut at the first link whose check cells are not detectable or fail direction.
chain: transits -> L1 (composite WCI, e=0.35) -> monthly mean -> L2 M1 (consumer goods) -> L3 M1, predicted inputs all the way; reported against realised at each stage, no pass rules of its own
overall: a link passes only if all four rules pass on the pooled check cells; M1 is primary, M2 reported as a rescue. Lab gate: tried only if a link passes its own check rules.
